Question: All the roots of the polynomial \[ \begin{aligned} &z^6-10z^5+Az^4+Bz^3\\ &\quad+Cz^2+Dz+16 \end{aligned} \] are positive integers, possibly repeated. What is the value of \(B?\)
Solution:
Use the coefficients to learn about the roots before trying to find them. If the six roots are \(r_1,\ldots,r_6\), the polynomial factors as \((z-r_1)\cdots(z-r_6)\), since its leading coefficient is \(1\). To obtain a \(z^5\) term, choose one negative root and five copies of \(z\); its coefficient is therefore \(-(r_1+\cdots+r_6)=-10\). The constant term chooses all six negative roots, so it is their positive product, \(r_1\cdots r_6=16\). Thus the roots have sum \(10\) and product \(16\).

Since their product is \(16=2^4\), every root is a power of \(2\). Start with six roots all equal to \(1\), whose sum is \(6\). Building product \(16\) requires four doublings. Each doubling increases the sum by at least \(1\), and it increases it by exactly \(1\) only when it changes a previously untouched \(1\) to \(2\). The sum is exactly \(6+4=10\), so all four doublings must be of different roots.

The roots are thus \(1,1,2,2,2,2\). To obtain the coefficient of \(z^3\) in the product of the six linear factors, choose three negative roots and three copies of \(z\). Every such product has a negative sign. Classify by how many roots equal \(1\) are chosen:
\[
B=-\left[\binom43\,2^3
+\binom21\binom42\,2^2
+\binom41\,2\right].
\]
These three contributions are \(32,48,8\), so \(B=\boxed{-88}\), choice A. Coefficients record sums of products of roots; the sign is determined by how many negative roots are selected.
